result:
I would rewire the ancient survival reflex that equates the unknown with danger, shifting the baseline instinct from fear to curiosity. 

That hair-trigger fear made sense when survival meant assuming every rustle in the tall grass was a predator. Now, it is an evolutionary hangover operating at a planetary scale. It is the invisible architecture behind tribalism, hoarding, willful ignorance, and almost every war. When faced with an unfamiliar culture, a contradictory idea, or an uncertain future, the default impulse is still to flinch, build a wall, or strike first.

I would not erase caution—self-preservation still matters. I would simply change the initial spark. If encountering the unfamiliar reliably triggered wonder instead of threat, humanity wouldn't need to be forced into empathy, sustainability, or peace. People would stop trying to conquer or erase what they do not understand, and start trying to actually know it. Everything else would fix itself from there.
